short: Heat shock factors bind the heat shock element (HSE), an array of the 5-base unit nGAAn in alternating orientation: nTTCn-nGAAn-nTTCn and longer runs. The DNA-binding domain is a winged helix, and HSF proteins trimerize through a coiled coil so that three subunits each read one 5-base unit, with further trimers loading cooperatively onto longer arrays. Humans have HSF1, HSF2, HSF4, HSF5 and the Y-linked HSFY1/HSFY2. HSF1 is the stress-inducible member, held inactive as a monomer until proteotoxic stress triggers trimerization. HSEs drive heat shock protein genes, and HSF1 activity also supports malignant transformation; HSF4 mutations cause congenital cataract.
long:
## The factors

Human HSF1 is the stress-responsive member, kept as an inactive monomer by intramolecular
coiled-coil interactions and by chaperone binding, and converted on proteotoxic stress into a
DNA-binding trimer that is further tuned by phosphorylation, acetylation and SUMOylation [PMID:20628411]. HSF2 is
developmentally and differentiation-regulated, binds many of the same elements, and forms
heterotrimers with HSF1 [PMID:17213196]. HSF4 is expressed mainly in lens and other epithelia and, unlike HSF1, is
constitutively trimeric and can act as a repressor at HSF1 targets [PMID:20628411]. HSF5 is poorly characterized
and largely testis-restricted. HSFY1 and HSFY2 lie in multicopy on the Y chromosome within the
AZFb interval and are expressed in testis [PMID:22158087]. All members share an N-terminal winged-helix DNA-binding
domain followed by hydrophobic repeats (HR-A/B) that mediate trimerization; the domain is among the
most conserved DNA-binding domains in eukaryotes.

## The motif

The recognition unit is 5 bases, nGAAn, and a functional heat shock element is an inverted array of
at least three of them [PMID:3146692,2590940]. The classical rendering is nTTCnnGAAnnTTCn; the two permutations,
head-to-head and tail-to-tail repeats of the 5-bp unit, bind with similar affinity and with
striking two-fold symmetry, which was the original evidence that the unit and not a longer
palindrome is the recognition module [PMID:2590940]. HSF binds arrays cooperatively, so four, five or six units
give progressively higher affinity and are common in strongly inducible promoters [PMID:1899357]. The crystal
structure of an HSF DNA-binding domain showed a three-helix bundle capped by a four-stranded
antiparallel beta sheet, a winged-helix variant of the helix-turn-helix motif [PMID:8284672], and the human HSF1
structure in complex with DNA showed how the trimer positions three such domains around the helix [PMID:26727489].
Each domain reads GAA in the major groove, so most of the information sits on the GAA/TTC triplets,
but the flanks are not free: the two positions just 5' of each GAA affect whether an element works
[PMID:3146692], and the in vitro models here fix them as the TA of TTCTAGAA, with a weaker CG preference
in GAAcgTTC. That is why database models for HSF1, HSF2 and
HSF4 look like TTCTAGAA-cg-TTC or aGAA-cg-TTCTAGAA: they are the same three-unit array written with
different phase and strand. The HSFY and HSF5 models are different in a real way, favoring TTCGAA
and CGTTCGAA arrangements, so the family separates loosely into an HSF1/2/4 group and an
HSFY/HSF5 group; overall cohesion (0.66) is the lowest in this batch. Within the HSF1/2/4 group no
member is distinguishable from sequence.

## Where it acts

HSEs are promoter-proximal at the classic targets: HSPA1A/HSPA1B, HSP90AA1, DNAJB1, HSPB1 and the
other chaperone and co-chaperone genes carry clustered HSEs within a few hundred bases of the
start site, usually with a paused RNA polymerase already engaged so that induction is a release
step rather than a recruitment step [PMID:35687139]. HSF1 is also found at thousands of distal enhancers, and the
enhancer repertoire differs between stress types: heat shock and oxidative stress drive HSF1 and
HSF2 to partly distinct gene and enhancer sets [PMID:35687139]. GAGA-type factors and, in mammals, SP1 and NF-Y
occupy the same promoters; NF-Y binds the CCAAT boxes of several heat shock promoters. In cancer
cells, HSF1 occupies a large set of non-chaperone genes that is distinct from the classical heat
shock program [PMID:22863008], and in tumor stroma it drives a separate program in cancer-associated fibroblasts.
HSF1 also localizes to sex chromatin during meiotic repression.

## Biology and disease

Hsf1-null mice are viable but lack thermotolerance, show tissue-specific failure of stress-inducible
chaperone expression [PMID:12112007], and develop demyelination and protein aggregate accumulation in the CNS;
Hsf1 is also required for oocyte meiosis. HSF1 activity extends lifespan in C. elegans together
with chaperones, linking the pathway to proteostasis in aging [PMID:20628411]. In cancer, HSF1 supports malignant
transformation through a transcriptional program distinct from the heat shock response [PMID:22863008], high
nuclear HSF1 predicts poor outcome in breast cancer, and loss of Hsf1 suppresses lymphoma in
p53-deficient mice. HSF4 mutations in the DNA-binding domain cause autosomal dominant lamellar and
Marner cataract [PMID:12089525], and a homozygous splice mutation causes recessive congenital cataract; Hsf4-null
mice develop cataract with reduced gamma-S-crystallin. HSF2 contributes to inducible hsp expression
through heterotrimerization with HSF1 rather than acting alone [PMID:17213196]. HSFY copy loss accompanies AZFb
deletions in azoospermia, though targeted studies argue HSFY genes are not themselves required for
spermatocyte maturation [PMID:22158087], so the association may be positional.

## Reading a hit

A three-unit HSE is reasonably informative, and models here reach 17-21 bits, so a good match is
worth following up. Two specific traps make this family riskier than that number suggests. First,
nGAAn arrays overlap other purine-rich motifs. A GGAA core is the ETS recognition sequence and
GGAAA is the NFAT core, so loose HSF models score on ETS and NFAT sites and vice versa; one
Vierstra archetype in this family is explicitly labelled HSF/NFATC for that reason. A single
nGAAn unit is worthless as evidence. Second, and more concretely, several ChIP-derived HSF1 models
in these collections are not HSEs at all but resemble the tRNA internal B-box promoter element
(GTTCGAANNC) [PMID:2109308]: consensus strings such as GGGTTCGAATCCC appear in CIS-BP, HOCOMOCO and Vierstra
entries labelled HSF1 or HSF, and these are the entries whose label agreement with the rest of the
family is lowest. Treat a GGGTTCGAATCC-like match as a possible tRNA gene rather than an HSE. The
evidence codes help: HSF1, HSF2 and HSF4 grade-A or grade-B models built on SELEX plus methyl-SELEX
(PSM, SM) give the canonical three-unit HSE, while the B-box-like models are ChIP-only (P). Finally,
a genuine HSE hit does not mean the gene is stress-inducible, because HSF2 and HSF4 occupy the same
elements constitutively and HSF4 can repress there.
caveats: The 5-base unit nGAAn is useless alone; require at least three alternating units. nGAAn arrays cross-score with ETS (GGAA) and NFAT (GGAAA) sites, and one archetype here is labelled HSF/NFATC for that reason. Several ChIP-only models labelled HSF1 or HSF match the tRNA B-box (GGGTTCGAATCC) rather than an HSE and have the lowest label agreement in the family; a hit of that shape may be a tRNA gene. The family also splits into an HSF1/2/4 group and a distinct HSFY/HSF5 group, and cohesion is the lowest in this batch. A hit does not imply stress-inducibility, since HSF2 and HSF4 bind the same elements constitutively.

timeline.finding: Deletion analysis of the Drosophila hsp70 promoter in COS cells shows that residues -47 to -66, upstream of the TATA box, are needed for heat-inducible transcription; the region carries a sequence shared by heat shock genes, and a synthetic copy of the inverted-repeat consensus CT-GAA-TTC-AG makes a heterologous promoter heat-inducible.
timeline.methods: Promoter deletion mutants, synthetic element transfer, transfection, S1 mapping
timeline.open: What bound the element, and whether the palindrome or a smaller unit was the recognition module.

timeline.finding: Heat shock elements are modular, built from GAA blocks in alternating orientation at 2-nucleotide intervals, giving a 5-nucleotide periodicity; functional elements need three or more blocks, and the two nucleotides upstream of each GAA affect competence.

The minimal site for stable binding by Drosophila HSF is an inverted repeat of the 5-bp unit nGAAn; head-to-head and tail-to-tail arrangements bind equally, footprints grow with each added unit, and cross-linking indicates HSF binds as a trimer.
timeline.methods: EMSA, DNase I footprinting, protein cross-linking

timeline.finding: HSF binding is cooperative both within a trimer and between trimers: occupying one of two adjacent trimer sites raises binding to the second by more than 2000-fold, explaining why strong heat shock promoters carry multiple elements.
The 1.8 A structure of the HSF DNA-binding domain is a three-helix bundle capped by a four-stranded antiparallel beta sheet, a variant of the helix-turn-helix fold.
timeline.open: The domain was solved without DNA, so base contacts were inferred.

timeline.finding: In highly malignant human cancer cells HSF1 drives a transcriptional program distinct from the heat shock response, including many non-chaperone genes, and the program is active in primary breast, colon and lung tumors and associated with metastasis and death.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, expression profiling, analysis of patient tumors

timeline.finding: Cocrystal structures of the human HSF1 DNA-binding domain with heat shock element DNA, compared with the paralogue Skn7, show that single amino acid changes in the domain can switch DNA-binding specificity, and support a model of the trimer embracing the element.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, comparative mutagenesis, structural modeling
timeline.open: Whether natural paralogues such as HSFY use such substitutions to read different sites.

timeline.finding: HSF1 and HSF2 bind distinct genes and enhancers in oxidative stress and heat shock, release paused RNA polymerase II at promoters, and HSF1 occupies many chaperone genes under oxidative stress without activating them.

open: The GGGTTCGAATCC-like models labelled HSF1 or HSF are ChIP-only and match the tRNA B-box, and whether they reflect genuine HSF1 occupancy at tRNA genes or contamination of HSF1 peak sets by heavily occupied tRNA loci has not been established.

Whether HSFY and HSF5 have their own specificity is not resolved: the in vitro HSFY1 models favor TTCGAA-type arrays unlike HSF1/2/4, and the two low-grade HSF5 models disagree with each other (ACGTTCYA versus AACATTCCA, the latter resembling a TEAD site); single-residue changes can switch HSF specificity, but in vivo targets of HSFY and HSF5 are unknown.
